[[Unión Española]] was the defending champion. {{TOC limit|4}} ==Format changes== For the 2013–14 season, the [[Asociación Nacional de Fútbol Profesional|ANFP]]'s Council of Club Presidents approved the return to the [[Apertura and Clausura]] format, without playoffs.{{cite web |url=http://www.anfp.cl/detalle_noticia.php?noticia=8846 |title=Consejo de clubes aprobó torneos para el 2011 |language=es |trans-title=Council of clubs approved the tournaments for 2011 |publisher=[[Asociación Nacional de Fútbol Profesional|ANFP]] |date=December 9, 2011 |access-date=December 29, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101212200559/http://anfp.cl/detalle_noticia.php?noticia=8846 |archive-date=2010-12-12 |url-status=dead }} ==Teams== Eighteen teams will be competing in the Primera División for the 2013–14 season, sixteen of whom are returning from the [[2013 Chilean Primera División season|2013 season]]. [[San Marcos de Arica]] was relegated last season after finishing 18th.
